items.title: Eastern Michigan Announces Change in Football Leadership
items.summary: Eastern Michigan University Athletics announced a change in leadership for its football program, ending Chris Creighton's 13-season tenure as head coach. A national search for the program's 38th head coach will begin immediately.

items.title: Football Grabs Thrilling Senior Night Win Over Kent State
items.summary: The night started with emotions as the Eastern Michigan University football team celebrated 31 members of the program on Senior Night, including 22 players, and finished with heartbreak before joy as the Eagles escaped their season finale with a thrilling 17-12 win over visiting Kent State University, Nov. 24, at 'The Factory' inside Rynearson Stadium in Ypsilanti. items.title: Know Before You Go: Eastern Michigan Hosts Kent State for Senior Night at The Factory
items.summary: Eastern Michigan University Football returns to The Factory for the final time in the 2026 season Tuesday, Nov. 24, when the Eagles host Mid-American Conference opponent Kent State University at 7 p.m. inside Rynearson Stadium.

items.title: Different Paths, One Team: EMU Football to Honor 22 Student-Athletes on Senior Day
items.summary: Their journeys to Eastern Michigan University took different routes. Some began their college careers in Ypsilanti and grew into leaders. Others arrived after competing at multiple universities, junior colleges, or programs across the country. Some found their role early, while others worked through seasons of development, new opportunities, and changing circumstances.

items.title: Eastern Comeback Bid Falls Short at Western Michigan
items.summary: Amareon Blue ran for a career-high 160 yards and three scores while the defense battled to help a second-half surge, but it was not enough as the Eastern Michigan University football team fell at Western Michigan University, 34-27, Tuesday, Nov. 17, inside Waldo Stadium in Kalamazoo, Mich.

items.title: Eastern Falls to Central Michigan in Motor City MACtion
items.summary: The Eastern Michigan University football team fell to visiting rival Central Michigan University, 35-7, in the Motor City MACtion game at Ford Field in Detroit on Nov. 5, as both teams opened their midweek competition schedule with the 104th meeting in the series. The Eagles fell to 4-6 overall, and 3-3 in Mid-American Conference play while the Chippewas improved to 4-5 overall and 2-3 in league play.
